You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testLANG_831` attempts to parse a date string using the pattern `"M E"`, expecting behavior consistent with `SimpleDateFormat`. The current bug report states that `FastDateParser` treats a single white-space in the pattern as matching any number of white-space characters during parsing, which is inconsistent with `SimpleDateFormat` that treats white-space literally without this special meaning. 

Looking at the `FastDateParser` class, the constructor `FastDateParser(String pattern, TimeZone timeZone, Locale locale)` initializes the parser and calls `init()`. In `init()`, the pattern is parsed into `Strategy` objects, with each strategy adding its relevant regex to the overall pattern using `addRegex()`. This regex pattern is compiled and used later during parsing.

The key method `escapeRegex(StringBuilder regex, String value, boolean unquote)` is used by `CopyQuotedStrategy` (the strategy used for quoted literal text) to append regex fragments for literal parts of the pattern. Inside `escapeRegex`, when a whitespace character is encountered, instead of appending a literal space regex (`\\s` or space character), the code appends `"\\s*+"` which matches zero or more whitespace characters (effectively "any number of white space" chars). This escape sequence behavior causes the parser to tolerate varying amounts of whitespace in the input string, differing from `SimpleDateFormat` which treats spaces as fixed literals.

Thus, the bug stems from `escapeRegex` converting each whitespace in the pattern to a regex that matches any number of whitespace characters (`\\s*+`). This is made evident by the loop checking `Character.isWhitespace(c)` and appending `"\\s*+"` to the regex. Consequently, when parsing, `FastDateParser` allows inputs with different amounts of whitespace than what the pattern literally has, causing parse successes for strings that would fail in `SimpleDateFormat`.

No recent bug reports directly relate to this whitespace handling issue. The root cause is specifically in `escapeRegex` in `FastDateParser` and how strategies build the regex used for parsing.

Recommended fix is to change the whitespace handling logic in `escapeRegex` so that whitespace is treated literally (matching exactly one space or the corresponding literal whitespace), consistent with `SimpleDateFormat`. This will make `FastDateParser` respect the exact presence and count of whitespace characters in patterns when parsing dates.

In summary, the failure and bug occur because `FastDateParser.escapeRegex()` replaces each whitespace in the pattern with a regex matching zero or more whitespaces, deviating from exact whitespace matching semantics of `SimpleDateFormat`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
